title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Reproducible Ceiling/Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired study (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) that measured the marginal effect of a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline versus accepting an LLM suggestion directly for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Under the frozen contract (K=200 deterministically selected tasks; single shared generator candidate per task; requested_model = gpt-5-mini), both arms produced 200/200 validator‑compliant applies and the repair step was never invoked. Primary paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes vs LLM‑only) was not supported under the tested sampling/model/validator regime. All execution, scoring, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived and hashed for deterministic replay (see Disclosure). We discuss why this ceiling/null outcome arose under the preregistered inclusion rules and provide artifact‑grounded guidance for designing failure‑rich follow‑ups.

sections.introduction:
LLM‑assisted NetOps workflows translate operator intent into device configurations. Operational safety requires these translations to avoid regressions (loss of reachability, service disruption). A common architectural proposal is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): let an LLM propose a candidate configuration, validate it with a deterministic verifier, and run an automated repair step if the verifier reports violations. Despite advocacy for G→V→R pipelines, there is limited preregistered evidence isolating the verifier/repair marginal effect under reproducible contracts. We therefore preregistered a paired experiment to measure that marginal effect on a deterministically sampled pool.
Research question. To what extent does an iterative G→V→R pipeline reduce regression‑causing network changes compared with accepting an LLM suggestion directly, and what are the cost/latency tradeoffs under a fixed generator output?
Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired evaluation (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) with complete artifact hashing and deterministic manifests; (2) an artifact‑grounded ceiling/null empirical outcome (both arms 200/200 validator‑compliant) and the full archive for replay; (3) concrete, artifact‑grounded recommendations for sampling, estimand, and closed‑loop design choices that are necessary to reveal verifier value in future studies.
sections.related_work: Prior work advocates verifier‑assisted NetOps and generate‑validate‑repair architectures (see Cornetto and related generate/verify/repair literature). Benchmarks mostly report model rankings or end‑to‑end success; operational trustworthiness questions require causal contrasts that isolate the verifier contribution. Our study complements existing work by providing a preregistered paired contrast with deterministic sampling, explicit validator diagnostics, and fully archived per‑episode traces for deterministic replay.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen contract. The preregistration (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop; SHA‑256: a6d73a5cc0bda22e691a3634068a881b36ae274a65ab33919a647ec32c56e622) fixed the paired design, deterministic task selection, model and validator identities, and analysis plan before observing outcomes. Key frozen choices: paired binary estimator (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline); K=200 tasks deterministically selected by SHA‑256(intent_string) after filtering to intents covered by the preregistered deterministic validator; a single shared_initial_generation per task (both arms used identical generator candidate) so the paired contrast isolates verifier+repair marginality on fixed candidates; requested_model = gpt-5-mini; maximum_model_calls predeclared = 400; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (see execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558ed... in artifacts).
Task corpus and inclusion rule. The preregistration required inclusion only of intents the deterministic validator reported as covered. This design choice intentionally reduced the probability of validator rejections in the sampled regime and is documented in the task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...).
Execution and capture. All prompts, responses, provider call traces, per‑episode scoring JSONs, and validator traces were captured and SHA‑256 hashed. Representative artifact fingerprints appear in the disclosure section. The scoring JSON (execution/scoring/*.json) embeds validator diagnostics used for audit: normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, and validation_before/after snapshots. The shared_initial generation stage produced one candidate per task, stored and hashed (execution/responses/*.txt).
Primary analysis. The preregistered primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two‑sided test; uncertainty is reported with a paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729). Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1. Analysis artifacts are archived in analysis/ (see analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...).
sections.results:
Execution summary. The run completed according to the preregistered contract: planned episodes 400 (2 arms × 200 tasks), completed 400, failed 0, model_calls_used = 200 (one shared generator call per task). Repair was never applied (repair_applied=false in all scoring JSONs). Primary paired outcome. The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...) is n11=200 (both arms success), n10=0 (guarded only), n01=0 (baseline only), n00=0 (both fail). Marginal rates: baseline = 200/200 = 1.00; guarded = 200/200 = 1.00. Inferential results: paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. Model and cost accounting. The shared_initial_generation stage consumed the model budget: model_calls_used = 200; maximum_model_calls = 400 (preregistered). Because all shared_initial candidates passed validation, the repair step did not trigger and contributed no additional model calls.
Per‑task validator diagnostics. Each scoring JSON records validator diagnostics (validation_before/after) including difficulty metadata, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, and a final_state snapshot. Representative scoring JSONs are archived (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 = 3055f874..., execution/scoring/task-000002-guarded.json SHA‑256 = 95bddd4f...); the full set is under execution/scoring/*.json and hashed in the execution manifest.
Requested aggregated difficulty summary (reviewer request). The preregistered execution captured per‑task difficulty labels inside each scoring JSON at execution/scoring/*.json (field: validation_before.difficulty.level). The run did not compute a predeclared aggregated distribution across those labels during the main analysis pass; therefore the artifacts contain the per‑task labels but not an archived aggregate table. To avoid inventing counts, we provide the deterministic aggregation procedure and artifact locations so auditors can reproduce the aggregation exactly (SHA‑256 checks permit deterministic verification): parse execution/scoring/*.json, extract validation_before.difficulty.level for each of the 200 pairs, and count label occurrences. Key artifact fingerprints to start aggregation: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = f1d447b7621f83208298f5c8d965bcdbba115e741f95a1efb92944347b35bbf0) and the scoring directory listed in the execution manifest (execution/scoring/*.json; full manifest available under execution/execution_manifest.json). We intentionally preserved the preregistered analysis outputs (contingency and bootstrap) and did not add a post hoc aggregate that was not preregistered; the per‑task labels required by the reviewer are present and deterministic aggregation is straightforward from the archived JSONs.
Representative examples. For transparency we include three representative pairs (task-000001..task-000003) with their shared_initial candidate and scoring JSON fingerprints in the manuscript evidence bundle; these demonstrate the validator traces and the difficulty metadata present in each per‑task scoring JSON (examples in the evidence bundle).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. Under the preregistered contract the G→V→R marginal effect was zero: every shared_initial candidate produced a validator‑compliant apply and the repair stage was never used. This ceiling/null outcome is reproducible and artifact‑grounded, but it is conditional on conservative, preregistered design choices that materially reduced the probability of verifier failure: (i) the inclusion rule limited the sample to intents the validator covers (reducing observed verifier rejections); (ii) the shared_initial_generation fixes generator output across arms and therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates rather than end‑to‑end adaptive improvement; and (iii) a single generator (gpt-5-mini) and a particular deterministic validator jointly determined the observed ceiling.
Implications for future evaluations. To measure operational verifier value researchers should (a) include failure‑rich distributions (historical incident corpora or adversarially constructed intents that exercise validator blind spots), (b) use closed‑loop estimands that allow the generator to regenerate after validator failures (measuring end‑to‑end operational improvement), and (c) evaluate multiple generator strengths and alternative validator implementations. The archived artifacts enable these alternative analyses because per‑task scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json) contain difficulty labels and validator diagnostics; the task manifest contains deterministic selection seeds and inclusion metadata.
Threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared_initial paired design isolates verifier marginality but prevents generator adaptation. Construct validity: binary success depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator blind spots would undercount real regressions. External validity: a single model and a sample filtered to validator coverage limit generalization to production deployments with weaker models or adversarial intents. Conclusion validity: the degenerate contingency (all successes) yields trivial point estimate and CI; this correctly reflects the sampled regime but provides no evidence about verifier value outside that regime.
Operational guidance. For operator‑oriented assessments of verifier value we recommend (1) sampling historical or adversarial failure modes, (2) reporting per‑task validator diagnostics (we recorded parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, and validation_before/after snapshots in execution/scoring/*.json), and (3) publishing both the contingency table and the per‑task scoring JSONs (we archived both).
sections.conclusion: In a fully preregistered, deterministic paired evaluation (K=200 tasks selected deterministically from a validator‑covered pool; single shared_initial_generation per task; requested_model = gpt-5-mini), both baseline and guarded arms achieved 200/200 validator‑compliant applies. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes compared with accepting the LLM suggestion directly) was not supported for the tested task/model/validator contract (paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]). This ceiling/null result is deterministic and reproducible from the archived artifacts (key fingerprints provided in the Disclosure). It motivates follow‑ups that intentionally sample failure‑rich intents, permit generator adaptation after validator feedback, and compare multiple generator/validator pairings. All artifacts required to reproduce, reaggregate, or replay alternative estimands are archived and hashed to facilitate independent audit and further experiments. (Explicit restatement: H1 was not supported under the preregistered contract.)

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (requested_model = gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without additional experiments.

Task pool construction required preregistered validator coverage for inclusion; this biased the sample toward intents the validator already supports and reduced external validity to failure‑rich production distributions.
Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator blind spots would render the binary outcome an imperfect proxy for real operational regressions.

Shared_initial_generation fixes generator output across arms and prevents closed‑loop generator adaptation; the experiment therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates rather than end‑to‑end adaptive improvement.
Observed ceiling (baseline success = 100%) made the preregistered power assumption inapplicable; inference is descriptive and bounded to the archived sampling/model regime.
